briefs.source_chain: Oil spike on Iran-escalation warnings + Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia -> broad Treasury selloff to multi-year/post-2007 highs, driven almost entirely by real yields not breakevens -> resilient US jobless-claims/new-home-sales data plus a strong German Ifo add hawkish pressure -> equities show negative breadth but Mag-7 gains cushion the S&P decline.
briefs.brief_chain: Oil's jump (Iran escalation, Houthi attack on Saudi) reignites the bond selloff, pushing 10yr/30yr yields to multi-decade highs -> author attributes the move to real yields not breakevens, arguing no added inflation concern and no fiscal driver, with a personal view that breakevens are too low -> Reuters Hormuz-deal headlines briefly pull Brent down but Iran's rival ceasefire proposal stays tied to the resisted June MoU -> resilient data adds hawkish pressure -> S&P breadth negative, Mag-7 limits the decline.

distortions.what: Brief frames the move as oil 'reignit[ing]' the selloff; source frames it as a continuing rout (Wednesday's slump plus Thursday's move = biggest 2-day rise).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same hawkish, yields-higher read either way.

distortions.what: Brief paraphrases Iran's ceasefire proposal as 'tied to a June MoU the US has resisted' vs source's 'still built around the June MoU which the US has been reluctant to return to.'

briefs.source_chain: Hot September PMI (input-cost inflation highest since 2020) + Brent back above $100 on Iran UN rhetoric + a 3.20bp-tailed 5Y auction + 5Y yield breaking 5% -> risk-off as the market re-prices under-priced terminal Fed funds -> JPM's Market Intel desk reads the PMI as ~5% real GDP growth, still supportive of nominal-GDP-linked SPX earnings, with bond vol (not yield level) the bigger equity risk -> desk stays tactically cautious pending 3 US/Iran scenarios this week, holding core long Tech (Mag7/Memory/Semis) vs short RTY plus a Brazil/LatAm long.
briefs.brief_chain: Hot PMI + oil back above $100 + weak 5Y auction + 5Y yield break of 5% trigger yesterday's risk-off, implying under-priced terminal Fed funds -> desk reads PMI as ~5% real GDP growth still buttressing nominal-GDP-linked SPX earnings despite inflation, strong balance sheets delaying a slowdown, bond vol as the bigger risk -> tactically cautious pending 3 scenarios this week (deal / no-deal-no-escalation / no-deal-escalation) -> core call: long Tech vs short RTY, plus Brazil/LatAm as an AI-fear hedge, US to tactically outperform DM.

distortions.what: Brief labels the Brazil/LatAm long an 'AI-fear hedge'; source frames it as a play investors rotate into if fear/uncertainty around AI pushes them toward non-AI names, not an explicit hedge label.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same trade (long Brazil/LatAm), same rationale.

distortions.what: Brief omits the desk's three stated reasons for staying cautious (inability of energy prices to stabilize, elevated bond vol, unclear positioning/factors).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — supporting detail, not the stance or the call itself.

briefs.source_chain: Weak 5Y/7Y Treasury auctions with falling indirect demand, echoed by weak UK gilt and French OAT/Bund spread moves, mark the 'gradual' phase of debt stress -> yields have disconnected from oil, pointing to growth/competition-for-capital as drivers, with hyperscaler AI financing needs landing in the same IG market as swelling Treasury supply -> hidden credit stress (deteriorating HY breadth despite tight OAS, private-credit gating without defaults) -> weak equity internals despite index highs -> Meta's Muse pop is expected to turn into a subsidized margin war as rivals ship copies within 6 months, with Meta expected to raise capital before Anthropic's IPO, echoing Alphabet -> separately, Hormuz oil flows are recovering (via ship-to-ship transfers) even as Iranian flows stay at zero, while refined-product/diesel capacity remains constrained, with a threatened US diesel export ban risking a further price spike abroad.
briefs.brief_chain: Weak 5Y/7Y auctions with falling indirect bids, plus UK gilt and French OAT/Bund spread stress, frame the note's 'gradually, then suddenly' bond-stress theme -> yield rise is read as more about growth and competition for capital than oil, because hyperscaler AI financing needs are landing in the same credit market as Treasury supply -> hidden credit stress (HY breadth deteriorating despite tight OAS, private-credit gating without defaults) -> weak equity internals despite index highs -> Meta's Muse pop expected to become a subsidized margin war, with Meta expected to raise capital before Anthropic's listing, following Alphabet -> separately, Hormuz oil flows have recovered but refined-product/diesel capacity stays constrained, with a US export ban risking a further price spike abroad.

distortions.what: Brief presents 'growth and competition for capital' as the note's single joint conclusion on what's driving yields; source's own real-yield-vs-swaps analysis leans toward calling it 'more of a growth story,' and it's a dissenting PM quote (not the author) who pushes the competition-for-capital/crowding-out framing.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — doesn't change the note's stance, a lean, or an invalidation; it's a nuance in whose view attributes which driver.

distortions.what: Brief compresses two separate analyst estimates (Morgan Stanley's $1.7T of the $3.2T data-center spend, JPMorgan's ~$2.1T broader financing need) into a single '$1.7-2.1T of credit-market supply' range.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same magnitude and implication, just merged into one figure.

distortions.what: Brief drops the 'highest since 2008' qualifier on the UK 10-year gilt hitting 5.3%.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — supporting color, not a figure whose status changes.

distortions.what: Brief says Hormuz oil flows 'have recovered' without noting the source's caveat that Iranian flows specifically remain at zero while overall flows near July highs via non-Iranian ship-to-ship transfers.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the headline point (oil flowing, problem is refined product) is unchanged.

briefs.source_chain: Oracle's force majeure notice on the Blue Owl-backed New Mexico data center is read as legal protection, not an exit, but signals rising execution risk in hyperscale AI builds and shows third-party AI infrastructure isn't the bond-like asset it can appear -> Anthropic's expanded Akamai CPU deal shows frontier-model demand spreading beyond GPUs -> two GIR pieces shift the AI capex debate from spending size to required revenue/ROIC (hyperscaler ROIC has fallen from 40% to 25%) -> bottom line: the AI trade stays supported but future returns should come from selective winners, not broad capex exposure.
briefs.brief_chain: Oracle's force majeure notice on the Blue Owl-backed Project Jupiter site is read as legal protection, not an exit, but signals rising execution risk in hyperscale AI builds and that third-party AI infrastructure isn't the bond-like asset it can appear -> Anthropic's expanded, ~$20bn Akamai CPU deal shows frontier demand spreading beyond GPUs -> two GIR pieces shift the debate from spend size to required ROIC/revenue (hyperscaler ROIC down from 40% to 25%) -> conclusion: AI trade stays supported, but future returns need selective winners, not broad capex exposure.

distortions.what: Brief compresses 'selective winners in infrastructure, data, cybersecurity and applications' to just 'selective winners.'
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the conclusion (avoid broad capex exposure, favor selective winners) is preserved.
